## 1 Introduction {#s-1}

### 1.1 Foreword {#s-1-1}

This document (NL-P-01) specifies common organisational, technical, operational, security and resilience requirements for Wallet Providers and PID Providers participating in the NL EUDI Wallet Certification Scheme ("Stelsel").

The structure of the provider requirements follows ETSI EN 319 401 V3.2.1. References in that standard to a Trust Service Provider or trust service have been adapted to the relevant Wallet Provider, PID Provider and provider service context. This document does not claim that Wallet Providers or PID Providers are trust service providers solely because this structure is used.

This document shall be read with NL-SYS-01 and the applicable provider certification scheme, NL-P-W for Wallet Providers or NL-P-P for PID Providers.

Role-specific lifecycle and fraud-management requirements remain in NL-P-W04* and NL-P-P04*. Productfunctional and product-cybersecurity requirements remain in NL-FS and NL-CS.

### 1.2 Scope {#s-1-2}

The document uses the control structure of ETSI EN 319 401 V3.2.1, adapted to the EUDI Wallet Provider and PID Provider context. Other NL-P*-requirement documents contain more specific requirements that apply in addition to this requirements document.

The certified scope includes the provider organisation and the people, processes, information, infrastructure, cloud and hosting services, cryptographic services, interfaces, suppliers and operational controls used to provide wallet or PID services.

For the Wallet Provider, this includes wallet onboarding, activation and wallet-unit lifecycle operations.

For the PID Provider, it includes identity proofing, PID issuance, binding, status, suspension, revocation and lifecycle operations.

In the NL-SYS-01 NL Certification System Framework, certification of Wallet Providers and certification of the PID Provider are separate subordinate certifications. For a Wallet Provider, these certificates form part of the assurance evidence used for the top-level certification and national admission decision. This document does not define that top-level certification decision, admission conditions, product-functional certification or wallet-solution cybersecurity certification.

This document lists the common organisational, policy, security, operational and resilience requirements to be met by an EUDI Wallet Provider and a PID Provider seeking and maintaining certification under the NL EUDI Wallet Certification System. The requirements constitute subsidiary normative requirements for the Wallet Provider Certification Scheme (NL-P-W) and the PID Provider Certification Scheme (NL-P-P).

## 2 Legal Basis & References {#s-2}

### 2.1 Legal Basis {#s-2-1}

The legal basis for these requirements is formed by the Union and applicable national legislation governing European Digital Identity Wallets, electronic identification, cybersecurity risk management and incident reporting.

The following instruments are particularly relevant:

- Regulation (EU) No 910/2014, as amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183, establishing the European Digital Identity Framework.
- Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2982 on protocols and interfaces supported by the European Digital Identity Framework.
- Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2979 on integrity and core functionalities of European Digital Identity Wallets.
- Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2977 on person identification data and electronic attestations of attributes.
- Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2981 on the certification of European Digital Identity Wallets
- Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2690, where the provider or certified service falls within its scope or where its technical and methodological requirements are adopted by the applicable national framework.
- Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2015/1502 concerning assurance levels for electronic identification means, including assurance level High.

Where national transposition or sector-specific rules impose more specific or stricter requirements, those requirements prevail. The applicant shall identify the competent authority, applicable reporting obligations and any sector-specific cybersecurity requirements relevant to its certified services.

### 2.2 Normative references {#s-2-2}

The following documents contain provisions which, through reference in this document, constitute requirements or criteria for its application. The latest applicable version adopted by the NL EUDI Wallet Certification System shall be used unless a specific version is stated:

- ISO/IEC 17065, Conformity assessment - Requirements for bodies certifying products, processes and services.
- ISO/IEC 17067, Conformity assessment - Fundamentals of product certification and guidelines for product certification schemes.
- ISO/IEC 27001, Information security management systems - Requirements.
- ISO/IEC 27002, Information security controls.
- ISO/IEC 27005, Guidance on managing information security risks.
- ETSI EN 319 401 V3.2.1 (2026-01), used as the baseline for the common provider controls in Chapters 4 to 7

## 3 Terms & Abbreviations {#s-3}

The key words "shall", "shall not", "should", "should not", "may", "need not", "will", "will not", "can" and "cannot" are interpreted in accordance with ETSI drafting rules. "Shall" identifies a mandatory certification requirement. Requirement identifiers are stable references for evaluation plans, evidence records, findings and certificates.

### 3.1 Terms {#s-3-1}

PID Provider: the legal entity responsible for identity proofing and issuing and managing PID for EUDI Wallet Units, including the PID-provider obligations allocated by NL-SYS-01 and NL-P-P.

Wallet Provider: the legal entity responsible for providing and operating the EUDI Wallet service and for the walletprovider obligations allocated by NL-SYS-01 and NL-P-W.

Certified scope: the provider role, services, locations, systems, processes, interfaces and outsourced activities covered by the provider certificate.

Provider service: the organisational and technical service, including supporting processes and dependencies, within the certified scope of a Wallet Provider or PID Provider.

provider: a Wallet Provider, a PID Provider, or both, according to the applicability of a requirement.

### 3.2 Abbreviations {#s-3-2}

- WSCD - Wallet Secure Cryptographic Device
- WSCA - Wallet Secure Cryptographic Application
- TSP - Trust Service Provider
- RTO - Recovery Time Objective
- RPO - Recovery Point Objective
- PID - Person Identification Data
- ISMS - Information Security Management System
- EUDIW - European Digital Identity Wallet
- CAB - Conformity Assessment Body

### 3.3 Symbols {#s-3-3}

No special symbols are defined.

## 4 Overview {#s-4}

Chapters 4 to 7 transpose the horizontal control domains of ETSI EN 319 401 V3.2.1 to Wallet Providers and PID Providers. Unless marked role-specific or conditional, each requirement applies to both provider roles and to all systems and outsourced services within their certified scope.

### 4.1 General {#s-4-1}

Provider conformity is assessed as service certification under the NL EUDI Wallet Certification System.

The Wallet Provider remains responsible for the secure provision and operation of wallet-related services and for maintaining valid assurance evidence for the wallet solution in scope.

The PID Provider remains responsible for controlled PID issuance, status and lifecycle management, and the supporting trust and fraud-management services within its certified scope.

## 5 Risk management framework and risk assessment {#s-5}

The Provider shall apply the risk-management framework and risk-assessment principles of ETSI EN 319 401 to the certified provider service, taking account of the NL-SYS-01 allocation of responsibilities, provider dependencies and the system risk register under NL-SYS-04.

| Requirement ID   | Normative requirement                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | Applies to   | Typical evidence                                 |
|------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------|--------------------------------------------------|

| REQ-5-02         | The framework shall define risk ownership, risk acceptance authority, assessment criteria, treatment options, review frequency and escalation thresholds.                                                                                              | Both         | Document review, interview and operating records |
| REQ-5-03         | The Provider shall maintain a current risk assessment addressing threats, vulnerabilities, dependencies and impacts affecting confidentiality, integrity, availability, authenticity, privacy and sole user control.                                   | Both         | Document review, interview and operating records |
| REQ-5-04         | The Provider shall map its assessment to the system risk register maintained under NL-SYS-04 and shall identify provider-specific additions, assumptions and residual risks.                                                                           | Both         | Document review, interview and operating records |
| REQ-5-05         | Risk assessment shall cover interfaces and dependencies between the Wallet Provider, PID Provider, wallet solution, WSCA/WSCD, trust services, access-certificate services, registration-certificate services and other material ecosystem components. | Both         | Document review, interview and operating records |
| REQ-5-06         | The Provider shall reassess risk following significant change, incident, vulnerability disclosure, material supplier change, threat-intelligence update or change to applicable legal or scheme requirements.                                          | Both         | Document review, interview and operating records |
| REQ-5-07         | Risk treatment decisions shall identify responsible owners, target dates, required evidence and residual-risk acceptance.                                                                                                                              | Both         | Document review, interview and operating records |
| REQ-5-08         | Risks that may affect certificate validity, subordinate assurance evidence, national admission conditions or another provider shall be reported in accordance with NL-SYS-01 and the applicable provider scheme.            | Both            | Document review, interview and operating records |
| REQ-5-09         | The Wallet Provider shall specifically assess risks arising from wallet onboarding, activation, binding to the user, wallet-unit lifecycle operations and integration with the designated PID Provider.                     | Wallet Provider | Document review, interview and operating records |
| REQ-5-10         | The PID Provider shall specifically assess risks arising from identity proofing, PID issuance, binding to a wallet unit, status services, revocation, fraud detection and dependencies shared by multiple Wallet Providers. | PID Provider    | Document review, interview and operating records |

## 6 Policies and practices {#s-6}

The Provider shall establish the policies, practice statements and terms needed to describe and govern its certified service. References in ETSI EN 319 401 to a Trust Service Practice Statement are implemented here as a Provider Practice Statement for the Wallet Provider or PID Provider.

| REQ-6.1-03       | The statement shall identify material deviations, limitations, assumptions and external services on which conformity depends.                                                               | Both         | Document review, interview and operating records |
| REQ-6.1-04       | The statement shall be approved by accountable management, version-controlled and reviewed at least annually and following material change.                                                 | Both         | Document review, interview and operating records |

## 7 Provider management and operation {#s-7}

The Provider shall implement and operate the management and technical controls in this chapter across its certified scope. The chapter follows the control sequence of clause 7 of ETSI EN 319 401 and applies it to wallet and PID service operations.

### 7.1 Internal organisation {#s-7-1}

Both provider roles shall apply the organisational governance, reliability and segregation-of-duties requirements of ETSI EN 319 401 clause 7.1 within their respective certified scope.

#### 7.1.1 General {#s-7-1-1}

| Requirement ID   | Normative requirement                                                                                                  | Applies to   | Typical evidence                                 |
|------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------|--------------------------------------------------|
| REQ-7.1-01       | The Provider shall maintain a documented organisational structure with clear accountability for the certified service. | Both         | Document review, interview and operating records |
| REQ-7.1-02       | Accountable management shall ensure adequate authority, budget, competence and independence for security, privacy, compliance, risk and incident-management functions. | Both         | Document review, interview and operating records |

#### 7.1.2 Organisation reliability {#s-7-1-2}

| Requirement ID   | Normative requirement                                                                                                                         | Applies to   | Typical evidence                                 |
|------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------|--------------------------------------------------|
| REQ-7.1-03       | The Provider shall identify conflicts of interest and implement controls to preserve trustworthy operation and impartial evidence production. | Both         | Document review, interview and operating records |

#### 7.1.3 Segregation of duties {#s-7-1-3}

| Requirement ID   | Normative requirement                                                                                                                                                                    | Applies to   | Typical evidence                                 |
|------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------|--------------------------------------------------|
| REQ-7.1-04       | Incompatible duties shall be segregated, including development and production administration, request and approval, key activation and key use, evidence creation and evidence approval. | Both         | Document review, interview and operating records |

### 7.2 Human resources {#s-7-2}

Both provider roles shall apply every personnel-security requirement of ETSI EN 319 401 clause 7.2 to employees, contractors, trusted roles and relevant supplier personnel supporting their respective certified scope.

| Requirement ID   | Normative requirement                                                                                                                                  | Applies to   | Typical evidence                                 |
|------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------|--------------------------------------------------|
| REQ-7.2-01       | Personnel and contractors in trusted roles shall be screened to a level proportionate to their access and responsibilities, subject to applicable law. | Both         | Document review, interview and operating records |
| REQ-7.2-02       | Role profiles shall define competence, authority, security responsibilities and required training.                                                                   | Both         | Document review, interview and operating records |
| REQ-7.2-03       | Personnel shall receive introduction and recurring training covering security, privacy, fraud, incident reporting, social engineering and role-specific procedures. | Both         | Document review, interview and operating records |
| REQ-7.2-04       | Access and responsibilities shall be reviewed when employment or assignment changes and revoked promptly upon termination.                                           | Both         | Document review, interview and operating records |
| REQ-7.2-05       | The Provider shall maintain sufficient staffing and succession arrangements for critical operations, incident response and crisis management.                        | Both         | Document review, interview and operating records |

### 7.5 Cryptographic controls {#s-7-5}

Both provider roles shall apply every cryptographic-control requirement of ETSI EN 319 401 clause 7.5. The Wallet Provider shall apply these controls to wallet-service and wallet-unit-related cryptographic assets under its control. The PID Provider shall apply them to PID issuance, signing or sealing, binding and status-service cryptographic assets under its control.

| Requirement ID   | Normative requirement                                                                                                                                                                    | Applies to   | Typical evidence                                 |
|------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------|--------------------------------------------------|
| REQ-7.5-01       | The Provider shall maintain a cryptographic policy covering approved algorithms, protocols, key lengths, key ownership, key lifecycle, certificate management and cryptographic agility. | Both         | Document review, interview and operating records |
| REQ-7.5-02       | Cryptographic keys shall be generated, stored, used, rotated, backed up, recovered, archived and destroyed under documented controls proportionate to their purpose.                     | Both         | Document review, interview and operating records |
| REQ-7.5-03       | Access to high-impact keys shall require strong authentication, separation of duties and tamper-resistant protection appropriate to the assessed risk.                                   | Both         | Document review, interview and operating records |
| REQ-7.5-04       | The Provider shall monitor deprecation of algorithms, protocols and cryptographic products and maintain a transition plan.                                                               | Both         | Document review, interview and operating records |
| REQ-7.5-05       | The PID Provider shall protect PID signing or sealing keys and associated status-service keys in accordance with applicable trust-service and scheme requirements.                      | PID Provider | Document review, interview and operating records |

| REQ-7.6-01       | Facilities hosting critical systems shall use layered physical access controls, monitoring, visitor management and access logging.                 | Both         | Document review, interview and operating records |
| REQ-7.6-02       | Environmental controls shall address power, fire, water, temperature, communications failure and other site-specific hazards.                      | Both         | Document review, interview and operating records |
| REQ-7.6-03       | Physical access rights shall be approved, reviewed and revoked, and anomalies shall be investigated.                                               | Both         | Document review, interview and operating records |
| REQ-7.6-04       | Where cloud or colocation facilities are used, the Provider shall obtain and assess evidence that physical and environmental requirements are met. | Both         | Document review, interview and operating records |

| REQ-7.7-02       | Changes shall be risk-assessed, authorised, tested, traceable and supported by rollback or recovery arrangements.                       | Both         | Document review, interview and operating records |
| REQ-7.7-03       | Development, test, acceptance and production environments shall be appropriately separated.                                             | Both         | Document review, interview and operating records |

| REQ-7.7-07       | Backup and restoration procedures shall be tested and shall preserve confidentiality, integrity and recoverability.                            | Both         | Document review, interview and operating records |
| REQ-7.7-08       | The Provider shall control production access by developers and shall record and review exceptional access.                                     | Both         | Document review, interview and operating records |

## Annex A (informative) Mapping to the eIDAS Regulation {#s-a}

### A.1 Purpose {#s-a-1}

This annex identifies how the provider-control domains support the legal and operational obligations applicable to EUDI Wallet Providers and PID Providers under Regulation (EU) No 910/2014 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183.

It is an aid to assessment and does not replace the legal text, the applicable implementing acts or the allocation of responsibilities in NL-SYS-01.

- Governance, risk and policy controls in Chapters 4 to 6 support demonstrable control of the provider service and its risks.
- Access control, cryptographic controls, operations, network security and incident management in Chapter 7 support protection of wallet and PID services and their evidence.
- Business continuity, termination and supply-chain controls support continued availability, orderly cessation and accountability for outsourced activities.
- Role-specific wallet-onboarding, wallet-lifecycle, identity-proofing and PID-lifecycle obligations remain governed by NL-P-W, NL-P-P and their subsidiary documents.

### A.2 Mapping {#s-a-2}

The mapping below supports traceability between Regulation (EU) No 910/2014, as amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183, and the provider controls in this document. It does not establish legal compliance by itself and does not replace the applicable provider scheme, implementing acts or legal assessment.

Role-specific wallet and PID lifecycle requirements remain in NL-P-W and NL-P-P. |

## Annex B (informative) Mapping to CIR 2024/2690 {#s-b}

### B.1 Introduction {#s-b-1}

This annex explains how the requirements in Chapters 4 to 7 support assessment against Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2690 where that Regulation applies to a Wallet Provider, PID Provider or supporting service within the certified scope. It is an assessment aid: it neither determines whether a Provider falls within the Regulation nor replaces the legal text, competent-authority supervision or a required conformity assessment.

Chapters 4 and 5 establish the control boundary and risk basis. Chapter 4 requires documented applicability decisions and responsibility allocation. Chapter 5 requires a maintained risk-management framework, current risk assessment, treatment and residual-risk decisions, reassessment after material events, and coverage of provider, ecosystem and supplier dependencies.

Chapter 6 establishes the governing documentation. The Provider Practice Statement describes the certified service, architecture, responsibilities, dependencies and implemented controls. Terms and conditions communicate relevant service conditions, while the information and network security policy establishes management-approved security governance, objectives, review and monitoring.

Chapter 7 provides the operational and technical control set. It covers organisation and personnel; assets and access; cryptography; physical, operational and network security; vulnerability and incident management; evidence; continuity and crisis management; termination; compliance; and supply-chain security. The requirement tables identify the applicable provider role and the typical evidence expected for assessment.

For assessment, the Provider and CAB should maintain one traceability matrix linking each applicable provision of Regulation (EU) 2024/2690 to the relevant Chapters 4 to 7 requirement identifiers, provider-scheme requirements, implemented controls, accountable owners and evidence. Evidence may be reused where it demonstrates both scheme conformity and regulatory implementation, but gaps in legal scope, role allocation or regulatory detail shall be assessed separately.

### B.2 Mapping {#s-b-2}

The mapping is intended to help avoid duplicate control implementation and duplicate evidence collection. It does not alter the scope of Regulation (EU) 2024/2690, determine whether a Provider is in scope, or replace an assessment required by competent authorities.

- Risk analysis and information-system security: Chapters 4, 5 and 6.
- Incident handling and reporting: Chapter 7.9.
- Business continuity and crisis management: Chapter 7.11.
- Supply-chain security: Chapter 7.14.
- Security in acquisition, development, maintenance and change: Chapters 7.3, 7.7 and 7.14.
- Assessment of effectiveness of controls and compliance: Chapters 7.10 and 7.13.
- Cyber-hygiene, personnel security and access control: Chapters 7.2 and 7.4.
- Cryptography and communications security: Chapters 7.5 and 7.8.
- Asset management and physical security: Chapters 7.3 and 7.6.
